BBIH Vision
Every learner feels safe, seen, and supported to thrive—equipped with the confidence, skills, and purpose to lead a happy, healthy, and successful life beyond school. While they’re with us, we want our students to: • Experience success. • Develop a positive attitude to learning. • Form goals for their future. • Belong to a community that values them as individuals
BBIH Mission
We exist to provide a second chance at education—through flexible, relational, and high-expectation teaching that empowers each learner to redefine what’s possible for themselves.
What makes us different:
• We are inclusive and empathetic • We offer a range of personalised pathways • We support students to become present and future-focused • We hold unwavering expectation that is the key to future success
• Leadership • Inclusion • Growth • Ambition • Sustainability

Careers Support
Careers Support at BBIH
At BBIH we are committed to ensuring that our students are prepared to move on to the next phase, be it further training, education or employment. Our personalised careers support programme has been designed to provide an environment where students can develop skills that will help them in the world of work as well as practical support such as help organising work experience.
The Career programme enables students to be fully equipped with the skills needed for further study and employment. Throughout the programme, students will develop an array of different skills and attributes.
All students will have access to careers guidance and advice that is impartial, informed and relevant. They will be exposed to opportunities and experiences that will allow them to further develop the skills and competencies required for a successful future, in whatever pathway they choose as an individual. The Career programme is designed to enable all students to be educated and able to make choices with regards to further/higher education, training and employment.

Our Expectations
We expect our staff and students to establish a safe and stimulating environment for students rooted in mutual respect and to manage behaviour effectively in accordance with the school’s behaviour policies. Teachers are expected to manage behaviour well and we emphasise the importance of consequences, certainty and consistency when re-shaping behaviour. We expect teachers to promote and maintain good professional relationships with students and to have clear rules and routines to promote good and courteous behaviour. It is the teacher’s responsibility to model the behaviour they want to see in their students.

A COMPELLING VISION FOR SUCCESS
A COMPELLING VISION OF SUCCESS
Curriculum Overview
At BBIH, our curriculum is designed to help every student feel safe, seen, and supported to thrive—academically, personally, and socially. Guided by our values of Leadership, Inclusion, Growth, Ambition, and Sustainability, we provide a curriculum that enables students to build the confidence, skills, and purpose they need to shape positive futures.
We understand that every student arrives with a different story. Our aim is to provide a broad, flexible, and personalised curriculum that meets each learner where they are—and help them move forward.
🔹 Core Curriculum Aims:
• Support students to make meaningful progress, both academically and personally • Offer tailored progression pathways into further education, apprenticeships, or employment • Reinforce a positive identity as a learner, with high expectations and individualised support
🔹 How We Deliver Our Curriculum:
• Consistency: No matter the subject, year group, or level, all students receive the same high-quality education. Lessons are structured, purposeful, and supportive. • Small class sizes: With an average class size of 12 or fewer, students benefit from strong relationships with subject specialists and regular, precise feedback that identifies how to improve and succeed. • Clear, actionable feedback: Teachers check learning continuously in every lesson, offering frequent feedback that helps students understand both what they’re doing well and what their next steps are. All work is checked weekly to ensure progress remains on track.
• Assessment that drives progress: o At Key Stage 3, regular use of clear descriptors enables teachers to pinpoint individual progress and guide improvement.
o At Key Stage 4, students work towards nationally recognised qualifications at a level suited to them, with assessment built into daily practice to support timely, targeted learning.
o At Key Stage 5, some of our most vulnerable learners are not yet ready to enter a large college environment due to academic suitability or social and emotional difficulties. Our combination of work-related experiences, including a day a week works experience alongside nationally recognised qualifications will enable them to transition successfully into the next stage of their lives.
We do not believe that a young person’s past should define their future. Our curriculum is ambitious and aspirational—giving every student the tools, qualifications, and self-belief to pursue their own version of success.
Calibre Curriculum
Developing the knowledge, skills and aptitudes that will be necessary for the next stage of the learning journey.
The planned learning experiences within the curriculum at Beacon Business Innovation Hub will allow our students to have aspirations and to be of the highest calibre.

100% of 11 students at BBIH have achieved qualifications in English and Maths and are progressing on to the next stage of their education at local colleges and sixth forms.
100% students pass vocational qualifications including some fantastic individual achievements.
Top achiever, Alex Pearce, gained a 4 in English Language and English Literature. A 5 in Maths and 55 in Science. Alex also successfully gained Level 2 qualifications in Finance, IT and Health and Social Care.
Keren Mutati started in February 2025 and achieved an impressive grade 5 in both English Language and Literature GCSE as well as Level 2 passes in Maths and Art.
Head of School, Kevin Howarth said
‘We are very proud of our students today, there is not one type of success and the fact that all of our students are leaving with qualifications in both English and Maths is something that makes us all feel proud. Our provision is about re-engaging young people. Students leaving us with 6 or 7 qualifications and consequently being able to progress is at the heart of what we do at BBIH.’
